judged_text: The fallback in showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error") is unreachable because message is a template literal that is non-empty on every code path. The 'unable_to_add_guests' string added to common.json in this same diff can never be displayed to anyone, and a failure with no err.data (network-level error) renders the literal toast 'undefined: <raw message>' — users hit by an error see a code-prefixed raw string or 'undefined: undefined' instead of the human-readable message the new key was added to provide.

The 'unable_to_add_guests' string added to common.json in this same diff can never be displayed to anyone, and a failure with no err.data (network-level error) renders the literal toast 'undefined: <raw message>' — users hit by an error see a code-prefixed raw string or 'undefined: undefined' instead of the human-readable message the new key was added to provide.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the `onError` handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. Because `message` is always a (non-empty) string due to being a template literal, the fallback `t("unable_to_add_guests")` can never be used. If `err.data?.code` is undefined (e.g., network/unknown error shape), the toast can become `"undefined: ..."`, which matches the finding and makes the newly added `unable_to_add_guests` translation effectively dead code.
